title: Homo erectus and early hominin dispersal out of Africa
summary: From about 1.9 million years ago hominins, among them Homo erectus, are dated at sites running from Algeria to Georgia, Java and northern China. The Dmanisi dates fall before the oldest African Homo erectus fossils, so where the species arose, and the order of its spread, remain debated.

uncertainty.note: Years are 1950 minus the age in years. Start: Ain Hanech "as early as 1.9 Ma" (Ferring et al. 2011), stone-tool evidence whose maker is not named. Dmanisi occupations 1.85-1.78 Ma. Java: 1.3-1.5 Ma (2020 uranium-lead and fission-track study); earlier argon-argon dates were 300,000-500,000 years older (Ferring et al. cite ca. 1.6 Ma for Java) and the Java chronology is contested. Earliest African Homo erectus is given by Ferring et al. as ca. 1.78 Ma, probably nearer 1.65 Ma; the Smithsonian gives the species range as about 1.89 million to 110,000 years ago. Zhoukoudian: 680,000-780,000 years (burial dating); older estimates were 230,000-500,000.

waypoints.label: Dmanisi, southern Georgian Caucasus: earliest dated occupations outside Africa and the Levant in this route, 1.85-1.78 Ma.

waypoints.date: between 1.3 million and 1.5 million years ago (Sangiran, Java; Archaeology magazine, 2020)
waypoints.label: Sangiran, Java: first appearance of Homo erectus dated 1.3-1.5 Ma by uranium-lead and fission-track dating; older argon-argon dates, 300,000-500,000 years earlier, had been used.

importance.justification: The first hominin dispersal into Eurasia, whose chronology reshapes where Homo erectus is thought to have originated.

reviewer_note: Least sure: Ain Hanech (the source says hominins, not Homo erectus, and the evidence is lithic); Java dates (1.3-1.5 Ma versus older argon dates); no East African waypoint because the earliest African erectus (ca. 1.78 Ma, per Ferring) is not later than Dmanisi and would reverse the route order. Coordinates are Wikidata, except Dmanisi (Ferring et al.).

beats.caption: Hominins are documented at Ain Hanech in Algeria as early as 1.9 million years ago, among the oldest evidence outside East Africa.
Occupation at Dmanisi, Georgia, dates to 1.85-1.78 Ma; Homo erectus reaches Java by 1.3-1.5 Ma, though older Java dates are argued.
By roughly 730,000 years ago hominins lived at Zhoukoudian in northern China, including during colder periods.
